The guild militia fights on foot with shields, spears and crossbows but is little drilled; hired cavalry decides campaigns. Vegetius is read in Tuscan. Foot have lately beaten knights abroad. Local: the sixteen militia companies (gonfaloni). Elsewhere: Swiss confederates (Laupen 1339); Flanders (Courtrai 1302); England, dismounted men-at-arms with archers (Crécy 1346).
- **Horse warfare (chariot, cavalry, horse archers)** [`cavalry_chariot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cavalry_chariot.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The armoured man-at-arms is the core of every army; Florence hires German and other mercenary horse. Hungarian mounted archers ride through Italy with King Louis in 1347–48.

The crossbow is the standard missile weapon of foot, walls and galleys. News of Crécy (1346) says English longbows outshot the hired Genoese crossbowmen. Local: crossbow makers; crossbowmen of the commune. Elsewhere: Genoa, crossbowmen for hire; England, longbow; Hungarians and Mongols, composite bow.
- **Mechanical artillery (torsion catapult, trebuchet)** [`torsion_artillery_trebuchet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/torsion_artillery_trebuchet.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Counterweight trebuchets are the siege artillery of the day, built on the spot by master carpenters. Ancient torsion engines are known only from Vegetius and Vitruvius. Local: master carpenters and engineers hired by the commune.

Galleys fight by boarding and crossbows; no rams, no guns. Florence has no fleet or port of its own and hires or allies for ships. Local: Pisa and Porto Pisano. - **Incendiary weapons and Greek fire** [`incendiaries_greek_fire`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/incendiaries_greek_fire.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Fire arrows and pots of pitch, sulphur and oil are used in sieges and at sea. Byzantine Greek fire is a legend.
- **Field fortification (marching camp, wagon fort, entrenchment)** [`field_fortification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/field_fortification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Armies camp behind ditches and palisades, and besiegers build fortified camps (bastie). Levied peasants dig. Reports say the English at Crécy fought from a prepared position.
- **Gunpowder (black powder)** [`gunpowder`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gunpowder.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Known to a few specialists and from Latin recipe books; made in small amounts as a loose meal. Saltpetre is scarce and dear, bought through Venice or from apothecaries. Local: apothecaries (Arte dei Medici e Speziali); masters of the commune's guns. Elsewhere: China, powder weapons of many kinds; Mamluk Egypt and Syria.
- **Cannon and artillery** [`cannon_artillery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cannon_artillery.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Florence ordered metal guns and iron balls in 1326. Guns are few and small, frightening more than breaching; walls fall to trebuchets and hunger. Villani reports English guns at Crécy. Local: bell founders; the commune's gun masters. Elsewhere: Calais, English guns at the siege (1346–47); China, bronze and iron cannon.
- **Ballistics and scientific gunnery** [`ballistics_gunnery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ballistics_gunnery.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Engineers range trebuchets by trial. Theory says a missile flies straight until its impressed force is spent, then falls. Elsewhere: Paris, Buridan's impetus theory.
- **Handguns and muskets (matchlock, flintlock)** [`handguns_muskets`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/handguns_muskets.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. No hand-held firearm is in service in Italy; the few guns are fixed pieces. Small hand guns appear in Italian records only in the 1360s. Elsewhere: China, metal hand cannon since the late 13th century.

Neither handguns nor drilled pike blocks exist here. Drill by word of command needs men kept under pay all year, which no commune does.
- **Socket bayonet** [`socket_bayonet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/socket_bayonet.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. There are no handguns for it to serve.
- **Bastioned fortification (trace italienne)** [`bastion_fortification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bastion_fortification.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Guns do not yet threaten walls, so nobody sees the need. Defence means height: Florence's new circuit (finished 1333) has tall thin curtains and towers. Local: third circle of walls (1284–1333).
- **Siegecraft, mining and counter-mining** [`siegecraft_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/siegecraft_mining.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Sieges are won by blockade, trebuchets, timber-propped mines, treachery and hunger. Calais held out eleven months against Edward III (1346–47). Elsewhere: Calais, the English siege.
- **Broadside gunnery and the line of battle** [`naval_gunnery_line_of_battle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/naval_gunnery_line_of_battle.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Sea fights are boarding actions between galleys under a hail of crossbow bolts. Guns are too small to harm a hull.
- **War rockets** [`war_rockets`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/war_rockets.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Latin recipe books mention 'flying fire'; no Italian army uses it and no fireworks are shown at feasts yet. Elsewhere: China, rockets in war.
- **Standing army, pay and supply** [`standing_army_logistics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standing_army_logistics.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. The commune hires companies by short contract for each war and dismisses them at peace; paying soldiers in peacetime looks like tyranny and waste. Roman legions are known from books. - **Mercenaries, militias and the loyalty of armed men** [`mercenaries_citizen_militia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mercenaries_citizen_militia.md) — K4, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Florence fights with hired foreign cavalry and fears it: Werner of Urslingen's Great Company plundered Tuscany in 1342. The guild militia mans walls and won the street fights of 1343. Local: the sixteen militia companies (gonfaloni); wartime commissions of citizens. Elsewhere: the Great Company, in 1347–48 with Louis of Hungary's army.
- **Conscription and the mass army** [`conscription_mass_army`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/conscription_mass_army.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Every citizen owes militia service in his company, and the contado sends foot and diggers. Rich men pay substitutes; long campaigns are left to mercenaries.
- **Camp hygiene and army health** [`military_camp_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/military_camp_hygiene.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept medium. Vegetius, read in Bono Giamboni's Tuscan, advises clean water and moving camp. In practice siege camps rot, and camp fevers are blamed on bad air. Elsewhere: Caffa 1346, plague in the besieging Mongol army; Calais 1346–47, sickness in the English camp.
- **Military engineering (roads, bridges, pioneers)** [`military_engineering_roads_bridges`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/military_engineering_roads_bridges.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. The commune hires master masons and carpenters as engineers for each campaign; labour is levied peasants. No permanent corps. Local: masters of the Opera del Duomo and the city walls. - **Strategy as a subject of study** [`strategy_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/strategy_theory.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Vegetius and Frontinus are the authorities, Vegetius also in Tuscan. Italian wars aim at ravaging, ransom and negotiated peace; captains avoid pitched battle. Local: Bono Giamboni's Tuscan Vegetius; chancery of the Signoria.

- **War games and operations research** [`wargaming_operations_research`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wargaming_operations_research.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Chess is the only war game, played keenly in Florence. Counting what actually worked would appeal to merchants who audit everything else.
- **Military intelligence and codebreaking** [`military_intelligence_codebreaking`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/military_intelligence_codebreaking.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Local: chancery of the Signoria; merchant company correspondents. Elsewhere: Avignon, papal chancery code lists; Mamluk chancery, Arabic treatises on breaking ciphers.
